originalTitle: Zambia vote counting resumes after pause over alleged attacks on polling staff
title: Exciting News from Zambia: Vote Counting is Back On!
content:
Hello amazing kids! It's me, Reporter Rafiki, your friendly news reporter for Africa! Today, we have super exciting news from a beautiful country called Zambia. You know how important it is for everyone to have a say? Well, something important happened in Zambia, and now it's all back on track!

What is a Vote?

Imagine you want to choose the best game to play with all your friends. Everyone gets to say what game they like the most, right? Well, in countries like Zambia, grown-ups do something very similar! It's called voting. They choose special people who they think will be good leaders. These leaders help make their country a safe and happy place for everyone, including all of you! Did you know? The word "vote" comes from an old Roman word that meant "wish" or "vow"! So, when people vote, they are showing their wish for their country.

The Big Voting Day in Zambia

Not long ago, it was a very special day in Zambia. People were excited to go to places called "polling stations." These are like special classrooms or community halls where grown-ups go to make their choice. They get a special paper, and on it, they mark the name of the person they want to be a leader.

What is a Ballot Paper?

This special paper is called a "ballot paper." It has the names of all the people who want to be leaders. Grown-ups carefully put a mark next to the person they want to choose. It's like picking your favourite colour or your favourite snack from a list! Each mark is a person's voice, saying who they want to lead.

Counting the Votes: The Important Part!

After everyone has voted and all the ballot papers are collected, the next big step is to count every single one of them. This is super, super important because it tells everyone who the people of Zambia have chosen to lead them. It's like counting the points in a game to see who won fairly! Everyone needs to know the correct score.

A Little Pause in Counting

But guess what? For a little while, something made the counting stop. Some naughty people tried to cause trouble and even took some of those very important ballot papers. These papers were already marked by the voters, which means people had already made their choices! This happened in a few places where the counting was happening. The people who were helping to count the votes are called "polling staff." They are like the helpers and referees of the election day, making sure everything goes smoothly and fairly. Did you know? Zambia is famous for its amazing Victoria Falls, which is one of the biggest waterfalls in the world! It's also called "Mosi-oa-Tunya," which means "The Smoke that Thunders."

Why Was This a Problem?

Taking marked ballot papers is not fair at all. It makes it very tricky and difficult to know exactly who people chose. Imagine if someone took away some of the points you scored in a game – it wouldn't be fair, right? You wouldn't know the real winner! So, the important people who organize the election had to be very careful to fix this problem.

The Super Good News! Counting Again!

But here's the super happy news! The important people in charge, who we call the "electoral commission," worked very hard to fix the problem. They are like the head referees for the whole election game! They made sure everything was safe and fair again. And guess what? They started counting all the votes again! Yay! This means that all the people's choices will be heard, and the right leaders will be chosen.

What is an Electoral Commission?

An "electoral commission" is a group of very important people. Their big job is to make sure that voting and counting votes are fair and honest for everyone. They are like the principal of a school, making sure everyone follows the rules so that everything is fair and works well.

Why is Counting Every Vote Important?

Counting every single vote properly is super, super important for Zambia. It shows that everyone's voice matters, no matter how small or big their wish is. When we count fairly, it means the people get to choose their leaders, and that's a very big deal in a free country. It means the country belongs to the people. Did you know? Zambia's national animal is the African fish eagle, which has a beautiful, loud call that can be heard far away! It's a symbol of freedom.

Zambia is Strong!

So, even with a small problem, Zambia is showing everyone that they are strong and can fix things when they go wrong. Soon, they will know who their new leaders are, chosen by the people. That's fantastic news for all the grown-ups and kids in Zambia! That's all for today from your news reporter, Reporter Rafiki! Stay tuned for more exciting news from our amazing continent, Africa!
summary: Vote counting in Zambia paused for a little while because some important voting papers were taken, but now the counting has started again so Zambia can choose its new leaders fairly.
whyMatters: This matters because counting every vote fairly helps the people of Zambia choose their own leaders, making their country strong and free, and ensuring everyone's voice is heard.

originalTitle: Who are the Chawinga sisters leading Malawi's bid for Wafcon glory?
title: Malawi's Amazing Football Sisters!
content:
Hello, hello, amazing friends! Reporter Kweli here, bringing you super exciting news from our wonderful continent, Africa! Today, we're going to talk about two very special sisters from a beautiful country called Malawi. They are doing something truly amazing in the world of football, and they are making everyone very, very proud!

Meet Our Stars: Tabitha and Temwa!

Let me introduce you to these incredible sisters. Their names are Tabitha and Temwa Chawinga. Can you say "Chawinga"? It's a special name, and soon, everyone will know it! Tabitha is the big sister, full of energy and amazing skills. Temwa is her younger sister, also super talented and fast! They are like a dream team, playing football together on the same big team for their country, Malawi. Isn't that just wonderful? They love playing football more than anything. They have spent so many hours practicing and getting better. Their love for the game shines through every time they step onto the field. Did you know? Having a sister or brother can be so much fun, especially when you share a hobby or play games together! It makes teamwork even more special.

What is Football?

For our friends who are learning about sports, let's quickly explain football! It's also known as soccer in some places. It's a game played with a round ball between two teams of players. The main goal is to kick the ball into the other team's net to score a point, which we call a "goal"! The team that scores more goals by the end of the game wins. It's a very popular game all over Africa and the world. It needs lots of running, kicking, passing, and most importantly, teamwork! Everyone works together to help their team. Did you know? Football is played with your feet, but the goalkeepers, who protect the net, are allowed to use their hands inside a special area called the penalty box!

Malawi: Their Home

Tabitha and Temwa come from a lovely country in southeastern Africa called Malawi. It's famous for its big, beautiful lake, Lake Malawi! People in Malawi are known for being very friendly and kind. That's why Malawi is sometimes called "The Warm Heart of Africa." Imagine living in a place with such warm people and a giant, sparkling lake! It's a place where many children love to play outside, and football is one of their favourite games. It's wonderful that Tabitha and Temwa are bringing so much joy to their home country. Did you know? Lake Malawi is one of the biggest lakes in Africa and is home to many kinds of colourful fish that you can't find anywhere else in the world!

Playing Together: Sisters on the Field!

What makes Tabitha and Temwa extra special is that they play for the same team, Malawi, and they are sisters! They are like best friends on the field, always looking out for each other. They pass the ball to each other with perfect timing. They help each other get into good positions to score goals. It's like they can read each other's minds! When you play with someone you know so well and love, it makes the game even more exciting and fun. Their teamwork is amazing to watch! Did you know? When sisters play on the same team, they often have a special understanding that helps them work even better together, almost like they have their own secret language on the field!

What is WAFCON?

Now, let's talk about the big competition they are playing in: WAFCON. It sounds like a big word, right? WAFCON stands for "Women's Africa Cup of Nations." It's a very, very big football tournament. Think of it like a huge party where all the best women's football teams from different African countries come together to play against each other. Only the strongest and most skilled teams get to play in WAFCON. And guess what? Malawi's team, with Tabitha and Temwa, has done incredibly well! They have played so bravely and skillfully that they have reached the *final* game! The final game is the most important match of the whole tournament, where the two best teams play to see who will be the champion! Did you know? Winning the WAFCON trophy is a huge honour, like winning a very special gold medal in a big race or competition!

Their Amazing Journey

Tabitha and Temwa worked very, very hard to get to where they are now. They started playing football when they were small children, just like some of you! They didn't just become good overnight. They practiced almost every single day. Kicking the ball, running fast, learning new tricks, and never giving up. Sometimes it was tough, and maybe they felt tired, but their big dream kept them going. Their dream was to play football for Malawi and make their country super proud. And now, that dream is coming true! They are showing everyone that girls can be amazing football players and achieve great things if they put their minds to it. Did you know? The Chawinga sisters are sometimes called 'Scoring Queens' because they are so good at scoring goals for their team!

Dreams Come True

Because of the amazing play of Tabitha and Temwa, Malawi's team has done something truly historic. They surprised everyone by playing so well and reaching the WAFCON final! This is a very, very big deal for their country. Imagine how excited everyone in Malawi must be, cheering for their team! Hooray for Tabitha and Temwa! They are showing young girls and boys everywhere in Africa and the world that if you work hard, believe in yourself, and follow your passion, your biggest dreams can absolutely come true. They are living proof! Did you know? Many famous athletes, musicians, and artists started practicing their skills when they were very young, just like these sisters!

Why They Are Special

Tabitha and Temwa are special for many reasons. They are not just fantastic football players; they are also wonderful role models. A role model is someone you look up to, someone who inspires you to be your best self. They show us that girls can be strong, brave, and successful in sports. They show us the power of teamwork, the importance of never giving up, and the joy of playing together, especially with family. They are making history for Malawi and for all of Africa! Did you know? When you work together as a team, you can achieve much bigger and better things than trying to do everything alone! It's like building a tall tower with many blocks – you need every block and every friend!

You Can Do It Too!

So, what can we learn from the incredible journey of Tabitha and Temwa? We learn that it's important to work hard for what you want. We learn to never, ever give up, even when things are tough. And we learn that our dreams, no matter how big, are important and worth chasing. Maybe one day, you will be a football star too! Or a brave doctor, a kind teacher, a brilliant scientist, or anything else you dream of being! Just like Tabitha and Temwa, keep practicing, keep learning new things, and keep believing in yourself. You are amazing! Go Malawi! Go Tabitha and Temwa! And go, you, my amazing friends! Thank you for listening to Reporter Kweli. See you next time for more exciting news!
summary: Sisters Tabitha and Temwa Chawinga are super football stars from Malawi, who have worked very hard to lead their country's team to the final game of a big competition called the Women's Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON).
whyMatters: This is important because Tabitha and Temwa are showing everyone that girls can be amazing football players, they are making Malawi very proud, and they inspire all children to work hard and follow their dreams.

originalTitle: Afghan women tell the BBC their lives are unrecognisable after five years of Taliban rule
title: Big Changes for Girls and Women in a Faraway Land
content:
Hello, Wonderful Friends!

Hello, wonderful friends! Your kid-friendly news reporter from Africa is here! Today, we're going to travel with our minds to a place very, very far away. It's a country called Afghanistan. It has tall mountains and warm sunshine, just like some parts of our beautiful Africa. But in Afghanistan, something sad has been happening for the girls and women there. Their lives have changed a lot, and not always for the better. We are going to learn about what life is like for them now.

What Happened in Afghanistan?

Imagine if all the grown-ups you know, like your mum, aunties, or big sisters, suddenly had to stop doing many things they loved. That's a little bit like what's happening in Afghanistan. About five years ago, a group of people called the Taliban took charge of the country. When they took charge, they made many new rules. These rules are very different from the rules we have here in Africa, and they make life very difficult for women and girls. Did you know? Afghanistan is a country in Asia! It's very far from Africa, but we can still send them kind thoughts and learn about them.

No More Jobs for Many Mums and Aunties

One of the biggest changes is about work. Here, our mums and aunties can be doctors, teachers, market sellers, or anything they dream of, right? They work hard and help our communities grow. In Afghanistan, many women used to have jobs like that too. They worked hard to help their families and build their communities. They were doctors, teachers, shopkeepers, and more. But now, with the new rules, many women are not allowed to go to their jobs anymore. Imagine if your mum suddenly couldn't go to work. It would be very hard for her to earn money to buy food, clothes, and school books for her children. This makes life very tough for families. Simple Explanation: Having a job means you earn money to buy important things like food and medicine. It also makes you feel happy and helpful! When women can't work, it hurts the whole family.

Girls Cannot Always Go to School

This is a really sad part for us, because we know how important school is! You all love learning new things, reading stories, and playing with your friends at school, don't you? School helps us grow smart and strong. In Afghanistan, many girls are not allowed to go to school anymore, especially after a certain age. This means they cannot learn to read and write well, or learn about maths and science. It's like a big door to knowledge has been closed for them. Boys can still go to school, but girls often cannot. Everyone, boys and girls, should have the chance to learn and grow! Learning helps you achieve your dreams and help others. Did you know? When girls go to school, they grow up to be amazing leaders, doctors, and teachers who help their whole country! It makes everyone's life better.

Strict Rules for Going Outside

Imagine you want to go to the market with your mum, or visit a friend. Here, you can usually do that freely and safely. But in Afghanistan, the rules are very strict for women. If a woman wants to leave her home, she often has to have a male family member, like her dad or brother, go with her. She cannot go alone. This makes it hard to do simple errands or visit sick relatives. She also has to wear special clothes that cover her whole body and face, so only her eyes show. This means it's hard for them to go out freely, even for simple things like buying food or visiting a sick neighbour. It feels like they are not free to move around easily. It's a very different way of living than what we know. Simple Explanation: Having freedom means you can choose what to do and where to go, as long as it's safe and kind. It means you can make your own choices about your life.

It's Harder to See a Doctor

When you feel sick, like you have a tummy ache or a fever, your mum takes you to see a doctor or a nurse, right? It’s very important to get help when you are not well, so you can get better. In Afghanistan, it has become much harder for women to get to a doctor or a hospital when they are sick. Sometimes, they cannot go alone, and sometimes there aren't enough women doctors or nurses allowed to work to help them. This means that if a mum or a girl gets very sick, it's harder for them to get the help they need to feel better. This can be very dangerous for their health. Everyone deserves to get well when they are sick. Did you know? Access to healthcare means everyone can see a doctor when they need to, which helps them stay healthy and strong! It's a very important right for all people.

Why Are the Rules So Strict?

The people in charge, the Taliban, believe these rules are correct for their country. They have a very different way of thinking about how women and girls should live. They believe this is the right way for their society. Many people around the world, and here in Africa, think that these rules are not fair. We believe that everyone, no matter if they are a boy or a girl, should have the chance to live a happy, healthy, and free life. We believe girls should go to school, women should have jobs, and everyone should be safe and able to see a doctor when they need one. These are important things for a good life.

What Can We Do?

Even though Afghanistan is far away, we can still think about the girls and women there. We can learn about different countries and understand that not everyone has the same chances. This helps us to be grateful for what we have. We can be grateful for our schools and our freedoms. And we can remember to always be kind to everyone, everywhere, and wish for a better future for all children. Learning about others helps us understand the world better. Let's hope that one day soon, girls and women in Afghanistan will have all the freedoms and chances they deserve. We can send our good thoughts and hopes for them! Did you know? Even small acts of kindness, like learning about others, can help make the world a better place for everyone!
summary: Girls and women in Afghanistan are facing many new and hard rules that stop them from going to school, having jobs, and getting help when they are sick, making their lives very different and difficult.
whyMatters: This matters because everyone, boys and girls, should be safe, happy, and free to learn and grow, no matter where they live in the world.
